notes: Libretto by Lorenzo Da Ponte (1787). Words follow the Schirmer vocal score's spelling and punctuation, and its repeats of words and lines. Where the print differs from the libretto the words follow the print: "scelerato" with one l (libretto scellerato; sung with ll), Don Giovanni's "Non sò più" (libretto "non so quel ch'io mi faccia", without più) and, in bar 56, "piu" printed without its accent; Leporello's "non si perdo, o si confondo" (libretto perde, confonde: the print gives him Don Giovanni's first-person forms). The score's "or-ren-do‿e ne-ro" is written here as the words orrendo, e, nero (the e elided onto orrendo on one note). IPA, word meanings and translations were drafted for this app (S32) and the IPA was checked against Castel. IPA follows sung Italian conventions: stressed syllable marked, elisions (two words on one note in the score) joined with ‿, open e/o as ɛ/ɔ. Translation literal, for meaning.
